summary: Repository initialized with docs/skills, agent pointers, Woven Dusk webfront, and utils layout.
why: Establishes canonical agent instructions and project structure before active development.

summary: Webfront scaffolded with React/Vite/Tailwind and Woven Dusk tokens. Starter skills migrated to docs/skills/. Agent pointers created for Claude, Codex, and Cursor.
why: Completes initialization plan with verified npm run build and uv run read-skills.

summary: Merged original DESIGN.md and woven-dusk SKILL.md into a single all-in-one design reference at docs/skills/woven-dusk-design/SKILL.md.
why: Consolidates Vercel/Geist structural guidance and Woven Dusk palette into one canonical document for agents and developers.

summary: Removed redundant docs/ and root markdown files. Consolidated workflow and project context into global-project-rules skill. docs/ now holds skills, changelog, and plans only.
why: Reduces duplicate documentation the user did not need.

summary: Added README.md, docs/purpose.md, and docs/goals.md with ReliaQuest grant context, architecture, five-phase timeline, and evaluation criteria. Updated global-project-rules and pyproject.toml.
why: Documents what Ariadne is and what the prototype must deliver by October 2026.

summary: Replaced high-level five-phase timeline with week-by-week roadmap (Wk 1-16) including ITS check-in, midpoint review, pitch workshop, and October ReliaQuest pitch milestones.
why: README and docs/goals.md now reflect the actual project schedule and task breakdown.

summary: Implemented a class-based DatasetDownloader in utils/download/ and wired it into main.py under a --download flag. Configured sequential job-specific logging (e.g. logs/1-download.log), updated pyproject dependencies with requests, and updated README.md Quick Start.
why: Integrates external MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC data acquisition into the repository CLI with persistent audit logs under logs/ of each execution.

summary: Pinned MITRE ATT&CK dataset version to v19.0 and CAPEC to v3.9 for reproducible evaluations. Restructured the download folders to be versioned (e.g. data/raw/attack/v19.0/) and added data/versions.json to track pinned versions in Git.
why: Ensures research and evaluation metrics remain completely reproducible across updates to the public data sources.

summary: Converted the roadmap tables in goals.md to checklists and marked the first two setup/download tasks as completed after verification.
why: Allows tracking project milestone progress in a clear checklist format.

summary: Added the Status column with checkboxes to the Roadmap tables in README.md, marking the first two setup tasks as completed.
why: Keeps the README roadmap synchronized with goals.md for consistent project status tracking.

summary: Fixed DatasetDownloader to decompress gzip-encoded HTTP responses when streaming to disk. GitHub raw serves ATT&CK JSON with Content-Encoding: gzip; writing response.raw without decode_content saved binary .json.gz data instead of plain JSON. Updated global-project-rules to require committing and pushing to GitHub after testing completes.
why: Downstream consumers expect valid enterprise-attack.json STIX, not gzip-compressed bytes with a .json extension. Agents should land verified work on GitHub promptly.

summary: Added an implementation plan for the ATT&CK Neo4j knowledge graph builder. The plan covers the build CLI contract, ATT&CK preprocessing into processed pairs, Neo4j graph artifacts, optional live loading, and validation phases.
why: Defines the next data-layer goal before implementation so the raw ATT&CK dataset can be converted reproducibly into a Neo4j fixture.

summary: Revised the ATT&CK graph builder plan to prioritize portable graph artifact generation before any database loading. The updated plan now centers on a normalized graph model, JSONL nodes and relationships, schema and constraint Cypher, Neo4j CSV files, and manifests.
why: Keeps the data-layer build reproducible and database-neutral so future experiments can swap graph backends after stable artifacts exist.

summary: Added the portable graph build CLI contract to main.py with --build attack|capec|all and --dry-run. Introduced utils/kg_builder as the artifact builder entry point and updated goals.md and README.md to describe the database-neutral ATT&CK artifact workflow.
why: Establishes the public build surface before implementing STIX normalization and artifact exporters.

summary: Added the artifact-focused KG builder package layout under utils/kg_builder with config, models, io, preprocess, schema, exporters, and validate modules plus KGBuildRunner orchestration stubs.
why: Organizes the build pipeline around raw input, normalized graph modeling, and portable artifact exporters before implementing ATT&CK loading.

summary: Implemented reproducible ATT&CK raw dataset discovery via data/versions.json and gzip-aware STIX bundle loading with source path, bundle id, object count, and version reporting. Added fixture and real-dataset loader tests.
why: Ensures the builder can locate and parse the pinned enterprise-attack.json before normalization.

summary: Implemented ATT&CK STIX preprocessing into a normalized graph model with node label mapping, relationship conversion, derived HAS_TECHNIQUE and HAS_SUBTECHNIQUE edges, and deprecated/revoked filtering. Added fixture and real-dataset preprocessing tests.
why: Establishes the database-neutral boundary and processed pairs checkpoint format for downstream artifact export.

summary: Wired the ATT&CK build pipeline to export nodes.jsonl, relationships.jsonl, schema.json, and manifest.json with endpoint validation and manifest counts tied to the processed pairs checkpoint.
why: Delivers the primary portable interchange format for later loaders and experiments.

summary: Added schema.cypher, constraints.cypher, and Neo4j CSV exporters generated from the normalized graph model with deterministic output and row-count checks against JSONL artifacts.
why: Prepares Neo4j-compatible import files without requiring a live database during the build phase.

summary: Added artifact validation for node uniqueness, relationship endpoints, label/type allowlists, deterministic ordering, manifest hash verification, and reproducibility across repeated builds.
why: Proves graph artifacts are internally consistent and reproducible before any database load phase.

summary: Added KG builder pytest suite, CLI regression tests, README artifact documentation, and deferred Neo4j loader notes. Documented the portable graph artifact workflow as the active Wk 3-4 data-layer deliverable.
why: Completes the reproducible ATT&CK artifact builder with tests and user-facing documentation.
